newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria traders shy away from new clearing system.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria traders shy away from new clearing system.

text.p: Share dealers watched proceedings at the Nigerian stock market on Monday rather than trade as a new computerised clearing system went into operation, an official of the exchange said.

The Central Securities Clearing System was commissioned on April 8 and is expected to speed up share transactions and clear the way for a rush of foreign investors, according to the stock exchange authorities.

"Only three brokers traded. Others watched to see how it would work out," Ndi Okereke-Onyuike, deputy director general of the bourse, told Reuters. "Turnover was low as a result; about two million naira," she said.
On a normal day, at least 40 traders sell and buy shares. Average daily turnover exceeds 50 million naira.
Okereke-Onyuike said most trading houses chose to watch because they did not want to be guinea pigs for the system.
"They (traders) did not believe they would be barred as we warned them unless they deposited share certificates to be traded with the clearing system," Okereke-Onyuike said.
None of the three houses who did business could be reached immediately for comments but those who failed to trade said they were apprehensive about the new system.
"It is not that we did not have money in our accounts to trade. We were watching to see how it works out," dealer Chuks Ohanwusi of Networth Securities said.
Others said the new system meant added financial burden on them because of the cost of complying with the latest procedure for lodging certificates before trading them.
Okereke-Onyuike said she expected activities to improve as dealers became more comfortable with the new system.
"People all over the world are usually apprehensive with a new system. Even the Canadians from whom we got it said they had the same experience with their own system," she added.
The clearing system, part financed with a United Nations Development Programme grant, is modelled after that of Alberta stock exchange in Canada.
